_comment: The turn-outcome rule, as a table both languages must satisfy.
The rule is implemented twice on purpose and neither copy can go: the server
derives outcome for the whole session (internal/chat/turns.go deriveTurnOutcome)
because the timeline rail must describe turns the paginated client store does
not hold, and the client derives the IN-FLIGHT turn's outcome
(static-src/turns.ts deriveOutcome) because no fetched summary can know a turn
that is still streaming.
This file is the contract between them. It is read by TestTurnOutcomeContract
(Go) and by turns.node.test.ts (TypeScript). Changing the rule in one language
fails the other language's test, which is the only mechanism keeping the two
in agreement — there is no code generation for behaviour.
`body` lists the turn's non-trigger messages. `refusal` true means the message
carries a refusal marker; `event` names an inline event's kind. `is_live` is
the caller's 'this is the last turn and the session is thinking' flag.
THE WRITER AND THE READER ARE ONE MECHANISM, so the tail clause below only
holds because persistOutcomeMarker skips nothing. It used to omit the carrier
for a clean prompted empty turn — the reader's default already said
`completed`, so the row looked redundant — which made a legitimately clean
empty turn byte-identical on disk to one a restart killed. Now every close
persists a carrier, so a body carrying no assistant message and no settled
outcome means NOTHING closed the turn, and `unknown` is a fact rather than a
guess. Restore the skip and the two `unknown` rows below become unreachable.
The predicate is 'no assistant message', not 'an empty body', and that is what
protects every turn already on disk: this chat file only ever gained an
assistant message at finalize, so a legacy turn carries one and still reads
`completed` — the row named for that carve-out is what stops a later reader
widening the clause.
ACCEPTED RESIDUAL, stated rather than fixed: a restart-killed turn whose
mid-turn compaction SEALED a segment does have an assistant message on disk
(SealTurnSegment -> segmentMessage), and that segment carries no outcome by
construction, so such a turn still reads `completed`. Stamping an outcome on a
segment would put two carriers in one turn and break the exactly-one-carrier
invariant.

cases.name: a clean finished turn
a turn nothing closed reads unknown, not completed
_comment: The reported population: a prompt refused after its user row landed, a cancel
during the spawn/prime/MCP window, and a process death mid-turn all persist the
user row and nothing else. This row used to want `completed`, which reported
every one of them as a turn that answered.

cases.name: a turn nothing closed YET is still running, not unknown
_comment: The live half, and why the clause sits below the isLive one: the carrier arrives
at finalize, so an in-flight turn legitimately has none and must not be reported
as an end nobody could read.

cases.name: a legacy turn with an assistant message and no outcome still completed
_comment: THE CARVE-OUT, and the row that stops a later reader widening the clause to
'an empty carrier'. Measured over the live records: 8 of the 14 carrier-less
turns are richly-answered legacy turns, two of them 185 and 265 blocks. Reading
those as failures would be a regression, not a fix.

cases.name: the live turn is running
a refusal fails the turn
a blocked infra-safety write fails the turn
a failed compaction fails the turn
a cancel interrupts the turn
an interrupt interrupts the turn
a refusal beats the running flag
an interrupt beats the running flag
failed beats interrupted when a turn carries both
failed beats interrupted regardless of order
a model switch is not an outcome
a successful compaction is not a FAILURE
_comment: This row's real property is that a compaction does not make a turn failed, and
that is unchanged. It wanted `completed` while an absent carrier defaulted that
way; a body holding one event row and no assistant message is now a turn nothing
closed, so it wants `unknown`. Either way the assertion worth having is that it
is not `failed`.

cases.name: a durable outcome is read, not inferred
a durable outcome beats the running flag
a cancelled turn says cancelled, not interrupted
a refusal recorded on the wire says refused
an unmapped stop reason says unknown rather than failed
a later settled outcome supersedes a fragment's unknown
a fragment inside a live turn reads as running
an interrupt beats a fragment's unknown
a truncated turn still completed
a legacy turn with no durable outcome still derives from its markers

_segmentation_comment: The BOUNDARY rule, and reviewers caught it wrong in both directions, so it is
pinned rather than described. A user message opens a turn; so does the first
persisted message of a turn with NO user trigger, which is derivable because a
Too narrow (only an empty turn's marker opens one) puts a non-empty
agent-initiated turn's outcome in the PREVIOUS turn's body, which can flip a
completed turn to failed on reload. Too broad (any non-user message opens one)
splits a prompted empty turn that has a user message to attach to.
An outcome of `unknown` does NOT close: it marks a fragment whose end never
arrived (a displaced wire turn's persist), and transcripts persisted before
the internal-tool suppression carry one per fresh session between the user
message and the real reply. Closing on it split that turn in two — a phantom
'Agent-initiated turn' holding the actual answer, and a rail one turn long.
`messages` is the flat persisted list. `want` is one entry per expected turn:
its opening message id, whether it has a user trigger, and its outcome.

segmentation.name: a prompted non-empty turn is one segment
a displaced boot fragment does not split its prompt's turn
a lone fragment keeps its unknown outcome
a prompted EMPTY turn is not split off from its own prompt
a non-empty agent-initiated turn's outcome does not land on the previous turn
an EMPTY agent-initiated turn is its own turn and appears in the index
an EMPTY agent-initiated COMPLETED turn is its own turn and appears in the index
_comment: `completed` is the derivation's default, which is why the marker is skipped
for a PROMPTED empty turn: its user message already represents it. A turn with
no trigger has nothing else at all, so skipping the marker there deleted the
turn — absent from the transcript and from the rail, while the live client had
been told it ended. The skip is therefore semantic (a persisted trigger
already represents this turn), never `outcome == completed`.

segmentation.name: an interrupt divider stays with the turn it describes
two agent-initiated turns in a row are two turns
a legacy transcript with no durable outcomes segments as it always did
